items.title: 'Cottage hospitals' could be a game-changer for rural Malaysia
items.summary: FEW healthcare ideas have the potential to deliver such immediate benefits to underserved communities as the Health Ministry's proposed cottage hospital initiative. Selected rural health clinics will be upgraded with observation wards and enhanced medical capabilities, allowing patients to receive a broader range of treatments closer to home. In his winding-up speech during the debate on the Supply Bill 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat recently, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the Health Ministry has identified four existing health clinics under the concept: Sungai Asap in Sarawak; Telupid and Nabawan in Sabah; and Tekek on Pulau Tioman, Pahang.

items.title: Chen probe upends Shanghai route to the top
items.summary: THE unexpected corruption investigation into Shanghai party chief Chen Jining, once seen as a strong contender for China's highest leadership body, challenges assumptions long used by diplomats and analysts to anticipate Beijing's opaque power moves. Experts said the Shanghai party secretary post, a position once held by both President Xi Jinping and former president Jiang Zemin, was a well-trodden route to the party's top leadership posts that now appeared much less predictable. Over nearly four decades, eight former Shanghai party chiefs were promoted to the Politburo Standing Committee.

items.title: Trump urges Putin to end 'military aggression' in Europe
items.summary: WEST PALM BEACH: US President Donald Trump said Thursday he had asked Vladimir Putin to "pull back all military aggression" against Europe, in a fresh shift in tone towards the Russian leader he called his friend just last week. Trump said he had made the request to Putin when they met in China last week, adding that he thought it would help lead to a deal to end Moscow's grinding war in Ukraine. Trump said he had done so "in the hopes that a Deal can be made between Russia and Ukraine, and made quickly."

items.title: NST Leader: Keeping online scammers at bay
items.summary: Scammers have found a sweet spot in exploiting trust and fear, routinely using online digital technology to deceive victims. Online fraud has cost Malaysians RM7.33 billion since 2023. Let's get something clear: online transactions and banking are generally safe, provided users exercise care and follow security rules.

items.title: Abdul Gani Patail: Prosecutor behind Malaysia's high-profile cases
items.summary: Among the high-profile prosecutions Abdul Gani handled were the corruption case involving former Sabah chief minister Datuk Joseph Pairin Kitingan in 1993 and the case involving the Al-Ma'unah militant group in 2000. Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar, who confirmed the news of his death, also extended his condolences to Abdul Gani's family. Abdul Gani was also part of the prosecution team in the 2006 murder case involving Mongolian national Altantuya Shaariibuu.

items.title: SPM candidate fractures left leg in accident en route to exam
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A student who was on his way to sit for the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination fractured his left leg after the motorcycle he was riding collided with a car in Jalan Bangsar Utama 1 this morning. The accident occurred around 6.55am as the student was travelling from Pantai Dalam towards SMK Bangsar. Kuala Lumpur Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department chief Assistant Commissioner Suffian Abdullah said preliminary investigations found that the car, driven by a 25-year-old woman travelling in the opposite direction, was believed to have turned right without giving way to the motorcycle.

items.title: MoH to take action over video of rats eating bean sprouts at Pudu Market
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Health Ministry will coordinate an integrated enforcement operation with relevant agencies following a viral video showing rats eating bean sprouts at a premises in Pudu Market. In a statement, the ministry said the operation would involve the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry, the Islamic Development Department of Malaysia (Jakim), the Immigration Department and Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL). It said the operation would focus on compliance with premises hygiene standards, food handling practices, raw material storage, cross-contamination risks and the effectiveness of pest control measures.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Thursday, November 26, 2026
items.summary: MISSED what happened today? Here's a glimpse at what happened throughout the country in photographs. [[nid:1586604]] [[nid:1586603]] [[nid:1586602]] [[nid:1586601]] [[nid:1586600]] [[nid:1586599]] © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Sabah SPM candidates not affected by power disruption
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: All 42,808 candidates sitting for the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination in Sabah have not been affected by the electricity disruption in the state's east coast since this morning. Sabah Education Department director Abidin Marjan said the examination, which began last Monday, had proceeded smoothly despite the power outage and flooding, particularly in Sook. "We hope that electricity supply to the affected examination centres will be restored by tomorrow.

items.title: KTMB cable theft in Penang disrupts northern train services
items.summary: KTMB said the theft was discovered during an inspection by its auxiliary police and have disrupted train services in the northern sector today. "KTMB, through its auxiliary police force, will continue to intensify patrols and security monitoring to protect railway infrastructure and ensure smooth train operations," it said in a Facebook post. KTMB called on members of the public with information on any suspicious activities along railway tracks to contact the KTMB Auxiliary Police Information Collection and Dissemination Centre at 03-2263 1194 or the police for further action.

items.title: 372 held, nearly RM50,000 worth of drugs seized in Perak operation
items.summary: IPOH: Police detained 372 people and seized drugs worth RM49,648.30 in a three-day statewide operation from Nov 23. Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the operation involved 25 senior officers and 223 personnel, and focused on curbing drug trafficking and abuse at identified hotspots. Alwi said three wanted individuals were also arrested, while two hardcore drug addicts were identified for action under Section 39C of the Dangerous Drug Act.

items.title: Budget 2027 passage marks key step in improving lives, says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The passage of the 2027 Budget by the Dewan Rakyat today marks an important step in the Madani government's efforts to improve the lives of the people. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the Budget also encompassed measures to strengthen the country's resilience and secure its future. The fifth budget under the Madani Government involves government allocations totalling RM459.8 billion, alongside RM25 billion in investments from government-linked investment companies (GLICs), RM11 billion in public-private investments and RM14.2 billion in investments from federal statutory bodies and Minister of Finance (Incorporated) (MOF Inc) companies.

items.title: Former attorney-general Abdul Gani Patail dies at 71
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former attorney-general Tan Sri Abdul Gani Patail has died at the age of 71. Abdul Gani's second child, Faezul Adzra Patail, told Bernama that his father died at Prince Court Medical Centre at 9.15pm. Abdul Gani, 71, a law graduate of Universiti Malaya (UM), was the first graduate of a local university to be appointed attorney-general.

items.title: Rapid KL bus catches fire on SUKE while en route to workshop for maintenance
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A Rapid KL bus caught fire on the Sungai Besi-Ulu Kelang Elevated Expressway (SUKE) near Bukit Segar here about 2pm today. Rapid KL said the bus, operated by Handal Indah Sdn Bhd under Rapid Bus Sdn Bhd, was not in service when the incident occurred. Rapid KL confirmed that the technician driving the bus was unharmed.

items.title: Ismail Lasim remains Negri Sembilan MB, says source
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Datuk Ismail Lasim will remain as Negri Sembilan menteri besar, according to a source. I was informed that Datuk Mail (Ismail) will remain as menteri besar," the source said tonight. This afternoon, Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir granted an audience to Ismail at Istana Hinggap.

items.title: Power restored in parts of Sandakan, Lahad Datu and Kunak
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Electricity supply has been restored to several areas in Sandakan, Lahad Datu and Kunak tonight following an outage caused by a disruption to the transmission line from the west coast. Sabah Electricity Sdn Bhd, in a statement, said the main areas in Sandakan where supply had been restored included Sandakan Sports Complex, Sandakan Prison, Utama Park Villa Phases 1 and 2, Garden Villa, Utama Sri Condo Blocks A and B, Utama Court, Jalan Sibuga, Taman Mawar and Taman Anggerik. In Lahad Datu, the main areas where supply had been restored included Lahad Datu Hospital, the Eastern Sabah Security Command (Esccom) office, Lahad Datu District Office, Lahad Datu District Police Headquarters, Lahad Datu Health Clinic, Lahad Datu District Council, Fish Market, People's Market, Taman Fajar and Jalan Tengah Nipah.

items.title: Six days to restore Sabah east coast grid, riverbank erosion caused tower collapse
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Sabah Electricity Sdn Bhd (Sabah Electricity) is targeting six days to fully restore the 275kV transmission grid supplying Sabah's east coast after a transmission tower collapsed in Ranau early today. Its chairman, Datuk Saadiah Aziz, said the grid was expected to be fully restored by Dec 2, following the reconnection of two affected transmission lines. "We hope everything goes smoothly so that electricity supply to consumers on the east coast can return to normal," she said in a press conference at Sabah Electricity's headquarters.

items.title: Govt wants listed companies to adopt RM3,400 living wage benchmark
items.summary: Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said fair and adequate wages would enable employees to meet their basic needs and maintain a decent standard of living. He said this could also contribute to greater workforce stability, better talent retention and higher productivity. Amir Hamzah also said companies must invest in developing their workforce capabilities, particularly in data analytics, sustainability and environmental, social and governance (ESG) reporting, climate finance and digital finance.

items.title: Nine Kelantan districts at risk of flooding until Nov 30
items.summary: According to the Kelantan Early Flood Forecast, updated at 8pm, the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) identified Jeli, Pasir Mas, Tanah Merah, Tumpat, Pasir Puteh, Bachok, Kota Bharu, Machang and Kuala Krai as areas at risk. DID said potential flood-affected areas include known flood hotspots, low-lying areas and risk zones along several major river basins in the state. The Golok River basin covers Jeli, Pasir Mas, Tanah Merah and Tumpat, while the Kelantan River basin involves Kota Bharu, Machang and Kuala Krai.

items.title: 'It breaks my heart': Father mourns 2 sons killed in crash
items.summary: KOTA BARU: "It was heartbreaking to see my two children lying there covered in blood," said Saiful Nizam Abdul Sani, 42, whose two sons were killed in a motorcycle crash in Kampung Bechah Tendong, Pasir Mas, today. Saiful Nizam said the accident occurred as Saiful Haikal was taking his two younger brothers home after picking them up from kindergarten and school. "Saiful Haider died at the scene, while Saiful Hayyan died on the way to HRPZ II.

items.title: Genting falls into the red in Q3 with RM161.4mil net loss
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Genting Bhd posted a net loss of RM161.4 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q3 FY26), compared with a net profit of RM30.3 million a year earlier. Genting's quarterly revenue rose 7.3 per cent to RM8.02 billion from RM7.48 billion. However, its Resorts World Sentosa and Resorts World Genting operations recorded lower revenue and Ebitda.

items.title: Teen believed to have lost control before crash killed 2 brothers
items.summary: District police chief Assistant Commissioner Mazlan Hassan said the three siblings were travelling home on a Yamaha LC110 when the motorcycle skidded along the Tendong-Bunut Susu road in Kampung Bechah about 2pm. "The impact threw all three off the motorcycle. Mazlan said the eldest brother, who was riding the motorcycle, sustained head injuries and remained under treatment at the same hospital.

items.title: Discipline teacher cleared of physical assault, jailed over sexual remarks
items.summary: TAWAU: A secondary school discipline teacher was acquitted by the Sessions Court today of physically sexually assaulting a 17-year-old student four years ago. Judge Ahmad Faizadh Yahaya imposed a one-year jail term for the offence, with an additional one-year jail term and two strokes of the cane under Section 16 of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017. The charge was framed under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, read together with Section 16 of the same Act.

items.title: Opposition leader questions Achi Jaya's Boustead Plantations bid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Opposition leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin says it is against the proposed takeover of Boustead Plantations Bhd by Achi Jaya Plantations Sdn Bhd, questioning the prospect of a strategic plantation asset coming under foreign ownership. Hamzah said the opposition will not support the proposed sale, claiming that Boustead Plantations was set to be acquired by a company owned by foreigners. Achi Jaya reportedly emerged ahead of competing bidders SD Guthrie Bhd and Tradewinds Plantation Bhd, both of which have substantially larger plantation operations.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - November 26, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Myanmar talks Malaysia will engage Myanmar over the 200,000 nationals living here, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Muhyiddin under fire Prosecutors say Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin ignored the source of RM25.3 million in Bersatu's accounts despite controlling its finances. Sedition charge Former Undang Luak Sungei Ujong, Datuk Mubarak Thahak, will be charged with sedition tomorrow.

items.title: From remote Batang Rajang to luxury tables: Sarawak’s prized empurau commands up to RM2,500 per kg
items.summary: SIBU, Nov 26 — The landing of an empurau weighing over 12 kilogrammes at the premises of Sarawak wild fish supplier Jeferry Siew Seng Kwong here proves that the species is not merely an ordinary river catch, but a luxury commodity worth tens of thousands of ringgit. For Jeferry, 41, the business is not merely about chasing profits through trading exotic fish, but also ensuring that every bit of hard work by local fishermen receives a fair and lucrative return. Apart from empurau, Jeferry’s business premises located at Jalan Long Bridge also supply various other freshwater species including patin buah, tapah, jelawat, semah, tengadak, terubuk, sebarau, giant freshwater prawns (udang galah), ketutu, and baung.

items.title: Teen gets warning after admitting to cyberbullying
items.summary: TAWAU: An 18-year-old student who pleaded guilty to uploading a 13-year-old girl's photograph on social media with threatening captions was discharged with a warning by the magistrate's court today. The court also ordered the return of his RM500 bail. The accused admitted that he had acted on impulse before obtaining the victim's photograph and uploading it to his Instagram Story with threatening captions.

items.title: 11 foreigners held over NYPD impersonation scam in KL
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have arrested 11 foreigners suspected of running an international online scam by posing as New York police officers in Bukit Ceylon on Tuesday. The raid was conducted by Dang Wangi police at 5pm on Tuesday. "In the same operation, the raiding team seized three sets of New York Police Department (NYPD) uniforms, a New York police logo signboard and a map of New York City, which were used to deceive victims contacted through video calls.

items.title: Dewan Rakyat passes 2027 Budget
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Dewan Rakyat today passed the Supply (Budget) Bill 2027 by a majority voice vote. The Bill was tabled by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on Oct 9. The fifth budget under the Madani government involves a government allocation of RM459.8 billion, alongside RM25 billion in investments from government-linked investment companies (GLICs), RM11 billion in public-private investments, and RM14.2 billion in investments by federal statutory bodies and Minister of Finance Incorporated companies.

items.title: Tengku Ampuan Afzan Hospital to reorganise parking, introduce valet service
items.summary: KUANTAN: The Health Ministry has appointed a private company to reorganise parking at Tengku Ampuan Afzan Hospital (HTAA), provide valet services and introduce parking fees as early as March. Pahang Public Works, Transport and Health Committee chairman Datuk Razali Kassim said the company was appointed effective Nov 1 to reorganise existing parking facilities and increase capacity for hospital staff and visitors. He said upgrading works on existing parking facilities within the hospital compound would be carried out during the first three months.

items.title: Power restored in parts of Tawau, Semporna and Telupid
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Electricity supply was restored to several areas in Tawau, Semporna and Telupid this afternoon following an outage caused by a disruption to the transmission line from the West Coast. Sabah Electricity Sdn Bhd said the areas in Tawau where supply had been restored included the Health Ministry clinic office and quarters, Taman Ambar Park, Taman Kuhara Jaya, Taman Hilltop along Jalan Kuhara and Hilltop Supermarket. Other areas included the United Armed Forces Camp and 516 Territorial Army Camp, Taman Ria 1 to 9, Uni Park Industrial, Taman Jen Loong and Taman Bunga Tulip.

items.title: Cybersecurity gets its own priority in Malaysia’s new National Security Policy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today launched the National Security Policy 2026–2030, outlining Malaysia’s security priorities for the next five years, with a new strategic focus on cybersecurity and technology. “Our approach and outlook towards security threats have changed. The National Security Policy 2026–2030 is a continuation of the previous 2021–2025 policy, which was based on the Comprehensive Security concept.

items.title: No reduction: Deputy minister clears the air over RM1b Education Ministry budget cut claims
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — The Ministry of Education (MOE) has denied claims that the government had cut its development allocation by RM1 billion in Budget 2027, saying that the amount had been transferred to its operating expenditure before it was agreed that the allocation would be restored. Deputy Education Minister Wong Kah Woh said following MOE’s application to the Ministry of Finance (MOF), the ministry’s development allocation would increase to RM6.515 billion from the previous RM5.515 billion. “Therefore, the MOE’s development allocation will now increase to RM6.515 billion from the previous RM5.515 billion, representing an increase of RM200 million compared with the 2026 development allocation,” he said.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan exco swearing-in ceremony set for 9am tomorrow
items.summary: Earlier today, Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi had an audience with the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, at Istana Hinggap here to discuss the ongoing political crisis in the state. The meeting, which lasted about an hour, was also attended by Umno deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, Barisan Nasional secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir, Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki and Umno Information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. Also present was Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim.

items.title: IGP says police investigating Tony Pua over Najib pardon post, Khoo Poay Tiong over Friday prayer remarks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Former Damansara MP Tony Pua and incumbent Kota Melaka MP Khoo Poay Tiong are under police investigation over their Facebook posts. Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the two DAP politicians are being investigated separately, with Pua related to the declassification of documents relating to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s pardon, Khoo on the closure of businesses in Kuala Terengganu during Friday prayers. Mohd Khalid said both cases were still at the investigation stage.

items.title: Three RMAF officers among six to be charged in Shah Alam tomorrow over drug smuggling using military assets
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Six individuals, comprising three Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) officers and three civilians, will be charged at the Shah Alam Magistrate’s Court tomorrow in connection with a drug smuggling case involving the use of military assets. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said all six suspects would be charged under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 following the referral of the investigation papers to the Attorney General’s Chambers. He said action would be taken against seven other suspects arrested in connection with the case under the Dangerous Drugs (Special Preventive Measures) Act 1985.

items.title: Diplomacy first on Myanmar refugees and South China Sea, Anwar says at national security policy launch
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today emphasised the importance of diplomacy in addressing regional security challenges, stressing the need to maintain strong ties with neighbouring countries. Speaking at the launch of the National Security Policy 2026 to 2030 today, Anwar said Malaysia must prioritise diplomacy and maintain good relations with its neighbours to address regional security challenges while ensuring its own defence capabilities remain strong. This includes maintaining diplomatic engagement with Myanmar to address longstanding issues surrounding the repatriation of refugees from Myanmar in Malaysia, as well as pushing, through Asean, for a Code of Conduct on the South China Sea.

items.title: Budget 2027 sails through Dewan Rakyat by voice vote, four weeks after Anwar’s CSA deal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — The Dewan Rakyat today passed the Supply Bill 2027 via a voice vote at its third reading, capping weeks of committee-stage debate. This is Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s fifth and biggest federal budget, although development spending is still lower than the record allocation announced for 2023, at RM97 billion. Of the RM459.8 billion direct federal allocation, RM376.8 billion is earmarked for operating expenditure while RM83 billion goes toward development.

items.title: DAP still contesting Sarawak polls, but non-Sarawakian ministers to stay off campaign trail, says Chong Chieng Jen
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 26 — DAP will go ahead and contest the state election, but non-Sarawakian DAP leaders who hold federal minister or deputy minister posts will stay out of the campaign, its state chief Chong Chieng Jen said today. “Sarawak DAP decides for Sarawak,” he said in a press statement. He said Sarawak DAP maintains its position to contest whichever seats it decides on in the coming election.

items.title: Hannah Yeoh’s pol-sec says ‘nothing to hide’ after giving MACC statement on KLSCAH lease
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Political secretary Yap Yee Vonne has said that nothing wrong was done in extending the Kuala Lumpur and Selangor Chinese Assembly Hall (KLSCAH) land lease, after assisting a Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) investigation into the matter today. Yap, who is political secretary to Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh, said she attended MACC’s Putrajaya headquarters with lawyer Sangeet Kaur Deo to help with the probe. “We did nothing wrong, and we have nothing to hide or fear,” she said in a Facebook statement.

items.title: Top 10 and counting: Anwar makes the cut in Asia Power Index
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has been ranked among the global top 10 leaders for effective political leadership in the Lowy Institute’s 2026 Asia Power Index. Chinese President Xi Jinping topped the political leadership rankings in the 2026 Asia Power Index, scoring 100 out of 100 for global diplomatic effectiveness. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi ranked second, while Japan’s Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese placed fourth and fifth, respectively.

items.title: Tawau, Sandakan, Lahad Datu airports keep flying on gensets after outage
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 26 — Operations at Tawau, Sandakan and Lahad Datu airports remain normal despite a power supply disruption on Sabah’s east coast, with all three airports currently running on generator sets (gensets). Malaysia Airports Holdings Berhad (Malaysia Airports) said the outage affected the three airports following electricity supply disruptions reported by Sabah Electricity in several areas of the state. Electricity transmission tower T313 in Ranau collapsed early this morning, affecting both transmission line circuits and disrupting electricity supply to Sabah’s east coast.

items.title: Heads up: Heavy rain and strong winds forecast for KL, Penang and eight other states tonight
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds across 10 states and Kuala Lumpur until 8 pm tonight. MetMalaysia, in a statement issued at 4.30 pm, said the warning covers all of Penang and Kuala Lumpur, as well as seven districts in Kedah, namely Kuala Muda, Sik, Pendang, Yan, Baling, Kulim and Bandar Baharu. In Perak, the warning covers Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang and Muallim.

items.title: Former Sungai Ujong undang to face sedition charge in Seremban tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Former Sungai Ujong undang Datuk Mubarak Thahak @ Dohak is expected to face a sedition charge at the Seremban Sessions Court tomorrow over statements he allegedly made earlier this year. Free Malaysia Today (FMT) reported that Mubarak would be charged before judge Tasnim Abu Bakar for allegedly uttering seditious statements. The alleged offence took place on April 19, 2026, at the Balai Undang Luak Sungai Ujong in Seremban.

items.title: MetMalaysia warns of continuous rain across Terengganu, parts of Kelantan until Sunday
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued an alert-level warning for continuous rain in several areas in Kelantan and throughout Terengganu until Sunday (Nov 29). MetMalaysia said in a statement that the warning in Kelantan covered Pasir Puteh, Bachok, Kota Bharu, Tumpat, Pasir Mas, Machang, Tanah Merah, Jeli and Kuala Krai. An analysis of weather forecast models indicates that wind convergence is expected over the eastern part of the Peninsula until Sunday, potentially bringing continuous rain to both states throughout the period.

items.title: ‘Cooperating, not submitting’: Anwar defends PKR’s decision to sit out Sarawak polls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has defended PKR’s decision not to contest the Sarawak state election, rejecting suggestions that the party was bowing to Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) to preserve political ties at the federal level. His remarks followed criticism from Sarawak DAP chairman Chong Chieng Jen, who accused PKR of “sacrificing democracy in Sarawak” to secure GPS’s continued support for the federal government. GPS, which governs Sarawak, is a key partner in Anwar’s federal administration.

items.title: No licence, no registration: Sabah wellness company fined RM30,000
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 26 — A company was fined RM30,000, in default six months’ imprisonment, by the Sessions Court here on Thursday for operating an unregistered private medical clinic. Judge Marlina Ibrahim handed down the sentence to Katalina Aesthetic & Wellness Sdn Bhd after its director pleaded guilty on the company’s behalf to establishing Katalina Aesthetic & Wellness without registration under Section 27 of the Private Healthcare Facilities and Services Act 1998. The court was informed that officers from the Sabah Health Department’s Private Medical Practice Control Section raided the premises on the said date, where staff failed to produce a clinic registration certificate or licence, and subsequently seized documents, medicines and machines.

items.title: Zahid hints at end to Negeri Sembilan political crisis after royal audience, says palace to announce decision
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR، Nov 26 — The Negeri Sembilan Palace is expected to announce its decision on the positions of the menteri besar and state executive councillors following a meeting between the state’s Ruler and senior Barisan Nasional (BN) leaders this afternoon. Deputy Prime Minister and BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi indicated that an agreement had been reached during the audience، but said the final decision rested with Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir. Zahid also indicated that the state’s political impasse could soon be resolved.

items.title: Malaysia keeps ex-prisoner reoffending rate at 11pc, among world’s best, says minister
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 26 — Malaysia recorded an average recidivism rate of 11 per cent among former prisoners nationwide this year, reflecting the effectiveness of rehabilitation programmes implemented by the Prisons Department. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the rate was measured over a three-year period after an inmate’s release, placing Malaysia among the best-performing countries internationally. Saifuddin Nasution said the Prisons Department must continue improving its rehabilitation modules rather than rest on its achievements, to prevent former inmates from reoffending.

items.title: Amir Hamzah says domestic air links remain priority, but no AirAsia bailout promised
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Domestic air connectivity remains a government priority, while AirAsia Group Bhd’s financial position continues to be monitored to ensure the country’s aviation ecosystem is not disrupted, Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said. The airports with the highest AirAsia passenger shares included Sandakan (80 per cent), Sibu (76 per cent), Bintulu and Tawau (74 per cent each), Kuching (69 per cent), Miri (66 per cent) and Kota Kinabalu (61 per cent). In Peninsular Malaysia, AirAsia also accounted for significant passenger shares in Johor (70 per cent), Terengganu (56 per cent), Langkawi (56 per cent), Alor Setar (49 per cent), Kelantan (46 per cent) and Penang (36 per cent).

items.title: Sacked ‘Inspector Sheila’ gets court nod to challenge dismissal, seeks reinstatement and back pay
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Former police inspector SK Sheila Sharon has secured permission from the High Court to challenge her dismissal from the force as she seeks reinstatement, back pay and damages. Sheila filed her application on October 29 through law firm M Manoharan & Co, naming former Deputy Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay, the police disciplinary board, the Police Force Commission and the Malaysian government as respondents. Sheila wants the court to quash the disciplinary decision and order her reinstatement to the police force with her rank of inspector intact.

items.title: Anwar says Putrajaya cuts new borrowing to RM70b, but legacy debts linger
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Nov 26 — The government has reduced its annual new borrowings from about RM100 billion when it took over the administration of the country to about RM70 billion currently, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. However, he said the government still had to service and repay legacy debts inherited from previous administrations, including those involving 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB), the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) and Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH). Anwar said the government had to pay nearly RM1 billion annually to settle Felda’s legacy debts, including about RM980 million.

items.title: Johor sets aside RM20.73m to reduce flood risks in 2027
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Nov 26 — The Johor state government has allocated RM20.73 million through the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) for initiatives aimed at reducing flood risks next year, said state Public Works, Transport, Infrastructure and Communications Committee chairman Mohamad Fazli Mohamad Salleh. He said the allocation covers several initiatives, including 12 studies valued at RM1.54 million, seven flood mitigation projects (RM1.61 million) and three drainage projects (RM1.2 million). “The allocation also covers four coastal zone projects (RM2.7 million), 14 river basin projects (RM5.58 million), 12 agricultural drainage projects (RM3.08 million), eight river estuary projects (RM2.52 million), as well as minor related works valued at RM2.5 million,” he said during the winding-up session of the Johor Budget 2027 debate at the state legislative assembly in Kota Iskandar today.

items.title: All eyes on Istana Hinggap as Zahid, Tok Mat meet Negeri Sembilan Ruler
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 26 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan arrived at Istana Hinggap here at 3pm for an audience with the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir. Earlier, Tuanku Muhriz arrived at the palace at about 1.30pm. Also present was Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim, who arrived at the palace at 1.18pm.

items.title: Home minister says police must apply law equally to both sides of political divide
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 26 — Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said police must investigate all reports regardless of political affiliation, following questions about the investigation involving former DAP MP Tony Pua over the alleged disclosure of Pardons Board meeting minutes concerning former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak. He said police must discharge their responsibilities without restrictions or favouritism to dispel perceptions that the authorities were more lenient towards government supporters. “The reality is that when a statement is made and a police report is lodged, the police open an investigation.

items.title: Johor launches MyJT transport app to help commuters track buses, plan journeys
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 26 — The newly introduced MyJohor Transport (MyJT) application aims to make public transport more reliable and convenient for commuters in the city, particularly bus passengers. Developed by Pengangkutan Awam Johor (PAJ), the app allows users to locate their nearest bus stops and check estimated bus arrival times. Johor Public Works, Transport, Infrastructure and Communications Committee chairman Mohamad Fazli Mohamad Salleh said a key feature of the application allows passengers using the Bas Muafakat Johor service to plan their journeys more accurately.

items.title: Terengganu’s ECRL races towards Dec 12 launch as project hits 99.5pc completion
items.summary: MARANG, Nov 26 — The construction of the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) project in Terengganu is nearing completion, with progress reaching an encouraging 99.54 per cent ahead of the commencement of commercial operations on Dec 12. Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, also the Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL) chairman, said the 242-kilometre (km) ECRL alignment in Terengganu comprises six stations, which will serve as new transportation hubs in the state. He said the Jerteh, Bandar Permaisuri, Kuala Terengganu and Kemasik stations would cater exclusively to passenger services, while the Dungun and Chukai stations would serve both passenger and cargo services.

items.title: Muhyiddin ‘chose to close his eyes’ over RM25.3m in Bersatu accounts, prosecution says
items.summary: At Muhyiddin’s power abuse trial today, the prosecution argued that the RM25.3 million was not a “bona fide” donation to Bersatu, but were instead rewards given after three Bumiputera contractors received government projects under the Jana Wibawa programme. Lead prosecutor Datuk Wan Shaharuddin Wan Ladin said Muhyiddin’s trial is the first-ever case in Malaysia involving a prime minister’s alleged power abuse for the financial benefit of its “associate”, Bersatu. Wan Shaharuddin said that Bersatu would not have received RM25.3 million if Muhyiddin was not both the prime minister and Bersatu president at the same time, and if he had not opened the way for the Bumiputera contractors to be considered for the projects.

items.title: Malaysia’s gender gap narrows in the workplace, but women still underrepresented in politics
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 26 — Malaysia’s gender gap narrowed slightly in 2025 as the Malaysia Gender Gap Index (MGGI) rose to 0.711 from 0.708 in 2024. DOSM said women’s labour force participation rate rose slightly to 56.6 per cent in 2025 from 56.5 per cent in 2024, while their mean monthly salaries and wages increased to RM3,635 from RM3,499. “The MGGI measures the gender gap between women and men in four areas, namely economic participation and opportunity, educational attainment, health and survival, and political empowerment,” DOSM said in its MGGI 2026 report released today.

items.title: Woman survives apparent fall from 21st floor of KL flats, in stable condition
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — A 29-year-old woman has survived an apparent fall from the 21st floor of a block of flats in Kuala Lumpur and is reported to be in stable condition in hospital. The incident involving the Indian national occurred this morning, Utusan Malaysia reported. Brickfields district police chief Assistant Commissioner Hoo Chang Hook said police were alerted at about 11.02am.
